reasoning: All 7 failure edits are kept as written, since failure patches take priority. The 12 success edits cover different patterns (partial names, epithets, trade names, colon clues, counting, quoted-title tails, no-answer archive hits), so they are kept as well. Several edits shared an insertion anchor, so I moved the success edits to other anchors to avoid ordering ambiguity. The colon-clue edit now follows the date+place bullet. The 'More examples' head-noun edit now follows 'If not, keep the head noun.' The team-name edit now follows the 'One of these <role/title>' bullet. I reworded the head-noun example so it defers to the 'would a trivia key accept the bare word' test. This keeps it consistent with the failure edit that drops suffix-style type words. I also fixed a garbled sentence in the epithet edit ('works too'). I dropped the merge_level field from every edit.

edits.target: If the list is of real people, answer with the team, state or other entity they share.
edits.content: - A clue that is just ONE catchphrase, exclamation, slogan or line of dialogue with no 'this ...' pointer ('"Yabba Dabba Do!"', '"D'oh!"', '"Eureka!"') asks for the SOURCE it belongs to: the TV series, film, character or speaker the passages tie it to ('The Flintstones'). Passages are full of titles that merely contain the phrase (e.g. 'I Yabba-Dabba Do!' is a TV movie spin-off of the series). Never echo the quote or a title built from its words. Apply the delete-clue-words test: if your answer contains the clue's words, step up to the parent franchise, series or person. Keep a leading 'The' when it is part of the show's standard title.

edits.target: The context passages about the topic usually reveal the link.
edits.content:
- A clue that is ONLY one bare proper noun with no verb ('Hamburg', 'Timonium') is category-style. Answer with the larger entity that the passages tie it to: a city or town -> its country (or state), a region or landmark -> its country. Never repeat the noun itself and never say the clue is incomplete.
- 'His / her' + a quoted title of a song, album, book or film ('"Shake It" is the last song on his 1983 album "Let's Dance"') asks for the CREATOR (David Bowie). Never answer with a title or item that already appears in the clue. Passages repeating the title next to a person's name give the answer.

- Some things have a plural standard name (bagpipes, scissors, pliers, trousers, glasses, bellows). Keep the plural form that the general article or passage titles use ('Bagpipes'), not a made-up singular ('Bagpipe').

edits.target: If the clue says 'this manicurist / this king / this dessert', do not append that role word to the answer.
edits.content: - Echo check, which also applies to answers copied from an archive line: if the clue already states the head noun ('this market', 'this party') and the archive or passage answer is 'bear market', answer only the missing modifier ('Bear'). For 'This character's name was Zeb, but they called him this', answer only the nickname ('Grandpa'), not 'Grandpa Zeb'. Never include a name or word the clue says is the OLD or given name.

edits.target: The 'do not repeat clue words' rule is for a separate modifier already stated in the clue ('hasty' + pudding).
edits.content: - Prefix-style type words belong to the standard name and are kept: 'Lake Superior' (not 'Superior') when the clue lists sibling lakes ('Huron, Ontario, Michigan, Erie & this one'), 'Mount Everest', 'Fort Knox'. Suffix-style type words ('Amazon River', 'Roanoke Island', 'Adirondack Mountains') are dropped when the bare name is standard and the clue does not use the word.

edits.target: Other named entities in the clue are anchors, never the answer.
edits.content: - 'The alliance / union / league / association / guild / chain of these <Xs>' ('the alliance of these Chinese businesses') asks for the generic MEMBER type, as a bare plural noun ('laundries'), not the organization's full name that the passages give ('Chinese Hand Laundry Alliance'). Find the passage naming the members' trade or type, and drop the nationality and organization words that the clue already states.

edits.target: Other clue details (diet, ingredient, cooking method) are just conditions on the generic dish.
edits.content: - The same holds when the modifier is a region, nationality or variant adjective and the noun is generic ('The Highland version of this instrument has a blowpipe, a chanter & 3 drones' -> 'Bagpipes'; 'the Bengal type of this animal' -> 'Tiger'). Passages are titled with the specific variant ('Great Highland Bagpipe'), but that variant contains the clue's own modifier. The answer is the PARENT thing the variant is a version of, as the general article title gives it.

edits.target: Still apply the person-name rule above.
edits.content: - Partial-name requests ('First name of the man who...', 'last name of', 'surname', 'nickname of', 'initials'): first identify the full person from the passages, then output ONLY the requested part ('Helmut', not 'Helmut Kohl'). Do not return the full name when the clue asks for a piece of it.

edits.target: Do not talk yourself out of a well-supported entity.
edits.content: - Epithet, tagline or quoted-phrase clues ('He's "America's Sherlock Holmes in Sneakers"', 'known as the "Sultan of Swat"', 'nature's most labor-intensive fruit'): the quoted phrase usually appears verbatim in many passages right beside one name or title. Answer with that adjacent entity ('Encyclopedia Brown', 'pomegranate'), as the passages write it, not with the epithet or a description. This works for fictional characters as well as for real people and for works.

- 'This trade name / brand name / nickname / slogan of X' (X = a drug, product or company): answer with ONE name, the one the passages put first or repeat most often ('methylphenidate ... known by this trade name' -> 'Ritalin'). Never answer with the generic name already in the clue, a list of brands, or a less-cited variant ('Concerta', 'Ritalin SR').

edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content: - When the passages only imply the answer (a person's biography page that never states the birthplace), combine the clue's type word ('this capital city') with the anchors the passages do give (Swedish family, Alfred Nobel born in Stockholm) and your own knowledge, and name the single entity of that type. Give it as a bare name ('Stockholm'). Never reply that the context does not say.

edits.target: not the event, the place or the date.
edits.content: - Colon-separated clues ('A knighted Englishman:The Golden Hind', 'A French painter: Water Lilies') have the form 'Descriptor: Anchor'. The anchor is a hint, not the answer. Answer with the entity that fits the descriptor AND that every passage ties to the anchor (the knighted Englishman who sailed the Golden Hind -> 'Sir Francis Drake'). Use the name form the passages repeat.

edits.target: answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content: - Descriptive / definition-style clues ('A house with floors that differ by about half a story', 'This soft central part of your teeth contains the nerves & blood vessels', 'This science of growing plants without soil...', 'common Arabic name which means "servant of Allah"') ask for the one standard term being defined. Look for a passage that repeats nearly the clue's wording, a glossary line, or a title/heading shared by several passages ('Hydroponic Systems'), and answer with the term it defines ('split-level', 'pulp', 'hydroponics') as a bare term, never a description. If the passages only describe it, use your own knowledge of the term. Ignore hedges and puns such as 'whether it's a fruit or vegetable'. For 'name meaning X', give the whole name the passages pair most often with that meaning ('Abdullah'), not a component ('Abdul') or a rarer variant. Copy a person's full name when the passages repeatedly pair it with the clue's anchor ('Sidney Poitier', not 'Poitier').

edits.target: Take the answer that follows the clue, even if the whole context is one short passage.
edits.content: - Quoted lyric, quote or idiom with a slot ('"The object of my affection can change my complexion from white" to this color'): find the passages that repeat the quoted words and copy the full words that follow them ('rosy red', not 'red'). The words belong to the quoted phrase.

edits.target: If not, keep the head noun.
edits.content: More examples: 'the largest museum of this institution' -> 'Smithsonian Institution'; 'this standard wind scale' -> 'Beaufort scale'. When the clue's type noun (institution, scale, empire) is the head of the entity's standard name, every passage writes it that way and the bare word would not be accepted as a key answer, keep it.

edits.target: - For titles, give the standard title without quotation marks and keep internal punctuation as written in the context ('M*A*S*H', not 'MASH film').
edits.content: - Exception to the delete-clue-words test: when the clue shows only the tail of a title or name in quotes, directly after 'this' ('his book about this "Express"', 'this "Gold"'), that quoted word is part of the answer. Give the full standard title as the passages show it ('The Polar Express', "Ulee's Gold"), not just the missing front part ('Polar'). The test is for separate modifiers the clue states outside the title.

edits.target: the answer is exactly one of the listed options, copied verbatim. Use the context to pick which.
edits.content: - Counting clues ('rise 5 ranks from Tenderfoot & you're one of these', 'the third king after X', 'two steps above Y'): find the passage that lists the ordered ladder or sequence, count exactly the stated number of steps from the named starting item, and answer with the item at that position, using its standard name ('Eagle Scout'). Check that you did not count the starting item itself.

edits.target: Do not choose one that fits only some.
edits.content: - A passage that repeats the clue word for word but gives no answer beside it is NOT a usable hit. This covers video titles, forum posts, quiz lists, search-result stubs, and archive pages that list clues WITHOUT answers (the clue is followed by the next category or clue, e.g. 'A comedienne: "Ball of Fire" LOSING, LOSING, & MORE LOSING: ...'). Neighbouring text there is another clue. Do not give up or guess from the clue alone. Read the other passages for the sentence that states the same fact with the missing word filled in ('...limited trick-or-treating on Halloween'), and use your own knowledge. For a 'Category: "quoted phrase"' clue, answer the member of that category the phrase points to (a nickname, film title or pun on a name: 'Ball of Fire' + comedienne -> Lucille Ball), confirmed by passages that pair the person with the phrase. A blank written as 'it' or 'this' in a clue like 'became the Duchess of it' is filled with the bare place or word the passages attach to the title ('York').

edits.target: not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content: - 'This team's <player>' wants the full team name as the passages give it, city plus nickname ('New York Giants'). Only a clue that names the team and asks for 'this city' wants the city alone. 'This <nationality> artist / author / actor' wants the person's usual first + last name ('Pablo Picasso'), not just a surname and not a long legal name with middle names or initials.
